predecessors.name: Kingdom of Georgia
predecessors.text: the Black Sea coast from the Bzyb to the Ingur, the Sharvashidzes' principality after the 1463 defeat of George VIII at Chikhori

successors.name: Russian Empire
successors.text: the principality, absorbed into the Russian Empire in 1864 after the Caucasian War; Prince Michael renounced his rights in November 1864

ledger.x: 1463: the Sharvashidzes found the Principality of Abkhazia.

c. 1700-1705: the Ghalidzga-Enguri strip passes to the Abkhazian house. 'in 1705 three brothers of the Abkhazian ruling family, surnamed Chachba' divided their land, 'the third, Murzaqan, the southern part (from the Ghalidzga to the R. Enguri)'; the page says Samurzakano 'was established as a fief ... in the early…
1727: a southern coastal strip leaves the Abkhazian shape (-1,540 km2).
1788: the strip lost in 1727 returns (+1,570 km2).
2 July 1810: Russian Marines storm Suhum-Kale and install Sefer-Bey.
1864: Russia ends the Principality of Abkhazia.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)
wars.outcome: Russia stormed Suhum-Kale in 1810 and, at Bucharest (28 May 1812), 'retained Sukhum-Kale on the Abkhazian coast' while Turkey regained Poti, Anapa and Akhalkalaki.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829)
wars.outcome: 'Strengthened Russia's position and split the Abkhaz elite along religious lines'; the Treaty of Adrianople is not mentioned on the Abkhazia page.

wars.name: Crimean War
wars.outcome: 'During the Crimean War (1853-1856), Russian forces evacuated Abkhazia, and Prince Michael (1822-1864) reportedly switched to the Ottomans.'

wars.name: Caucasian War
wars.outcome: 'Russia subjugated the western Caucasus highlanders in 1864' and Prince Michael was forced to renounce his rights in November 1864, ending the principality.

certainty.note: A coastal principality whose inland limit lies in the Caucasus foothills and whose southern limit moved with the Mingrelian and Ottoman frontiers; no treaty or survey lines on the pages.
